intro: Here, on the Tigris, lies Hasankeyf, an ancient city in Batman province. The river splits this historic town in two, and its story stretches from the 1st millennium BC to the 20th century AD, while its cave settlements reach back many thousands of years further still.
history: People have lived in the caves beside the Tigris since the Neolithic era. Later, Hasankeyf rose to become a capital under the Artuqids and the Akkoyunlu. Then, in 2020, the waters of the Ilısu Dam covered part of the old town. But look up: the citadel still stands.
structure-1: You are now looking at Hasankeyf Citadel, the high citadel above the Tigris, with its cave settlements. Imagine the generations who made their homes in this rock.
structure-4: Here is the Tigris Bridge, the historic bridge of Hasankeyf. Its piers survive today, still standing in the river and recalling the crossing they once carried.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Great Palace and the Great Mosque, and save time for the Rock-cut Tombs.
facts: Did you know? Caves along the Tigris at Hasankeyf show evidence of settlement some 12,000 years old. That 12,000-year-old settlement was largely submerged by the Ilısu dam in 2020. One monument made a journey of its own: the tomb of Zeynel Bey was lifted whole and moved to new ground. The Artuqid bridge was reckoned the widest-spanning in the Middle East of its day, and its piers still break the water. And thousands of cave dwellings were cut into the cliff; some were still lived in during the twentieth century.
outro: This brings our tour of Hasankeyf to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This town has already lost much to the water; let what remains wait for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
